question: For the political education of the people at the local level, who brought the resolution on local self-government?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Ripon.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Ripon** brought the resolution on** local self-government** in India in** 1882.**
 
• This resolution is also known as the **Ripon Resolution or the Resolution on Local Self-Government.**
 
• This resolution aimed to** transfer some powers and responsibilities **from the British government to the local bodies or municipalities.
 
• This resolution was a significant step towards** decentralization and democratization** of the Indian political system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Mayo** was the Viceroy of India from **1869 to 1872,** before Lord Ripon.

 
 
• Lord Mayo established the **Land-improvement Act **and the **Departments of Revenue, Agriculture, and Commerce** on **June 9, 1871.**
 
• He made a strong case for Indians' need for a **basic education.** 
 
 
 
• **Lord Canning** was the Governor-General of India during the** Indian Rebellion of 1857.**
 
 
• **​**After the Indian government was transferred from the** British East India Company to the crown,** Canning oversaw its reorganization.
 
• In **1859**, he was granted an **earldom.**
 
• He reorganized his executive council by instituting departmental distribution of responsibilities through the** Indian Councils Act of 1861**.
 
 
 
• **Lord Lytton** was the Viceroy of India from** 1876 to 1880**, after Lord Northbrook.
 
 
• Because of the way he handled the** Second Anglo-Afghan War** and the** Great Indian Famine **of **1876–1878**, he is widely considered as a merciless viceroy.
